title: Non-LLM periphery/adjacency scout for the knowledge graph (plan only)
description:
PLAN ONLY. No runtime work. Ryan wants quantitative, NON-LLM graph methods to find things ADJACENT to the Papyrus knowledge base that sit toward the OUTER PERIPHERY of the graph, not the dense middle the catalog already clusters on. Output is a human-reviewable suggestion list that feeds the include/exclude gate (PPY-9272c8). A high score must never auto-accept a source. Wiki is not evidence.

Feasibility verdict: FEASIBLE. The graph is real, typed, attributed, and already has graph-analytics plumbing (weighted PageRank, relation-type weighting, in-memory graph builder, signals CLI). Every existing metric ranks toward the CENTER (PageRank, popularity, trending, authority). Nothing surfaces the periphery. That is the gap. Primary risk is corpus size (the architecture doc warns the corpus is small because of the human curation gate); periphery shells on a small graph are noisy, so measure before shipping and report stability.

See comments for: the graph we run on, candidate algorithms, data inventory (have vs add), the recommended first feature, and risks.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
## 1. The graph we run on (verified in code, not invented)

There are three candidate substrates. Only one is the right shape.

**A. Main knowledge graph — RUN ON THIS.** `SemanticNode` + `SemanticRelation` in `amplify/data/schema.ts:1345` and `amplify/data/schema.ts:1530`. Nodes are concepts/entities (`nodeKey`, `nodeKind`, `displayName`, `aliases`, `corpusId`, versioned lineage). Edges are typed directed relations with `predicate`, `relationTypeKey`, `relationDomain`, `score`, `confidence`. The vocabulary (~40 types across knowledge/ontology/evidence/classification/curation domains) is seeded from `corpora/papyrus-semantic-relation-types.yml`. The graph is materialized from Biblicus graph exports by `src/papyrus_content/analysis_graph.py`: reference→entity `mentions` edges plus entity↔entity ontology edges (`related_to`, `broader_than`, `same_as`, …) and reference↔reference `cites`/`authored_by`. This is a heterogeneous, attributed, typed, directed multigraph — exactly the 'dense middle' the Researcher describes.

**B. Local-pod wiki — NOT a graph substrate.** `pods/<pub>` + `src/papyrus/operator/pod_references.py`: `stories/<id>/idea.md`, `stories/<id>/references/*.json` (status/url/why/corus), `project/issues/*.json` (Kanbus), `pod-references.json`. This is a flat list of references attached to stories, not a dense graph. It is where the Researcher scouts finds and where a suggestion list would land — a *consumer* of the periphery report, not the substrate to run periphery algorithms on.

**C. Project wiki (`project/wiki/*.md`) — NOT a substrate.** A handful of orientation docs with markdown links. Too small and not a knowledge graph.

Verdict: run periphery/adjacency algorithms on (A). Emit suggestions into (B) and a wiki view.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
## 2. Candidate algorithms (non-LLM, deterministic; 2–4)

All run on the same in-memory graph that `rank_concepts` (`src/papyrus_content/ontology_enrichment.py:476`) already builds. All are O(|V|+|E|) or O(iterations·|E|). None call an LLM.

**Algorithm 1 — k-core / k-shell decomposition.** Iteratively peel nodes of degree ≤ k; each node gets a shell number = the k at which it survives. Outer shells (low k) that are still attached to the core = under-developed branches. Surfaces: concepts on the outer shell adjacent to the dense core. Cheapest, most standard, most interpretable. Pure Python, ~40 lines.

**Algorithm 2 — Personalized PageRank distance from the accepted core.** Seed PPR teleport mass on the current top-N authority concepts (the existing `authorityRank` top-K already on `SemanticNode`). Rank nodes by LOW PPR mass (or by symmetric commute time). Surfaces: concepts reachable from the core but that the core's attention 'leaks' away from — adjacent, not central. Reuses the existing `compute_pagerank` (`ontology_enrichment.py:608`) with a non-uniform teleport vector — a ~10-line change.

**Algorithm 3 — Classical core–periphery score (Borgatti–Everett / Rombach).** Fit a continuous periphery score per node; high-periphery nodes still attached to core nodes are the frontier. Surfaces: one periphery score per node, directly comparable to the existing `authorityScore`. Medium effort.

**Algorithm 4 (defer) — Community detection + boundary rank.** Louvain/label-propagation, then rank nodes on community boundaries (high inter-community betweenness, low internal degree). Surfaces: bridge concepts between communities. Heavier; defer until 1–2 prove useful.

**Complementary family — link prediction (Adamic-Adar / Jaccard / preferential attachment).** Run over reference↔concept and concept↔concept pairs that are NOT yet edges. Surfaces 'almost connected' sources — the natural scout targets. Cheap, pairwise, stdlib. This is the adjacency half of the request; algorithms 1–3 are the periphery half.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
## 3. Data inventory — what we have vs. what we add

**Already have (no new models, no new schema):**
- `SemanticNode` / `SemanticRelation` graph + Biblicus graph-export import (`analysis_graph.py`).
- In-memory graph builder: `load_ontology_state` / `load_live_state(models=[...])` (`ontology_enrichment.py:392`, `coverage_theme.py`).
- Weighted PageRank with dangling-node handling: `compute_pagerank` (`ontology_enrichment.py:608`).
- Relation-type weighting + operational-relation filtering: `RELATION_WEIGHTS`, `OPERATIONAL_RELATION_TYPES`, `relation_weight` (`ontology_enrichment.py:38–59`).
- Authority scoring already denormalized onto nodes: `authorityScore`, `authorityRank`, `acceptedReferenceMentionCount`, `distinctSourceKindCount`, `relationCount` on `SemanticNode`.
- Signals CLI surface: `papyrus knowledge signals concept-report --report-type {popularity,trending,pagerank}` (`src/papyrus_newsroom/cli.py:359`).
- Consumer: `papyrus editions plan` / `coverage_theme.py` already reads pagerank to pick CENTRAL coverage concepts.
- BFS graph expansion in the query engine (`services.py:519`, depth ≤ 3, topK ≤ 100).
- Embeddings exist (S3 Vectors, `ontology_concept_profile`) — but per Ryan's constraint, NOT used as the periphery signal.

**Would add (periphery layer only; reuses the graph builder):**
- A periphery score per node: k-shell number + core-periphery score + PPR-distance-from-core. Stored as a derived report (like the existing concept-report), optionally denormalized onto `SemanticNode` as a `peripheryScore`/`frontierRank` (mirrors how `authorityScore` is stored).
- A new `--report-type frontier` (or a sibling `signals frontier-report`) on the existing signals CLI.
- Link-prediction scores (Adamic-Adar/Jaccard) over non-edges → "almost connected" reference↔concept suggestion pairs.
- A wiki view + CLI emit of a human-reviewable suggestion list (the consumer surface).
- A stability indicator (bootstrap over edge perturbation) so humans see noise on a small corpus.

**Would NOT add:** no new GraphQL models, no LLM calls, no embedding-based density, no auto-accept, no auto-write of wiki pages.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
## 4. Recommended first Papyrus feature (one, human-usable, suggestion-list only)

**`papyrus knowledge signals frontier-report --corpus-key <k> --top <N>`** — a CLI + wiki-view "frontier suggestions" report.

It computes, on the existing `SemanticNode`/`SemanticRelation` graph, the two cheapest most-standard signals:
1. **k-shell number** per concept (Algorithm 1), and
2. **Personalized-PageRank distance from the current top-K authority core** (Algorithm 2, reusing `compute_pagerank` with a seeded teleport vector).

Plus a complementary **Adamic-Adar "almost connected" reference↔concept** list (the adjacency half).

It emits a ranked **suggestion list** of periphery concepts (and the references that already mention them, plus "almost connected" candidate references) for a human to review. A wiki page renders the top suggestions as a skimmable list beside the edition, in the same passive-steering style as the existing category-register pages.

**Why this one:**
- Reuses the in-memory graph builder and `compute_pagerank` that `rank_concepts` already constructs — minimal new code.
- Lives in the CLI/Python tooling path (`src/papyrus_content` / `src/papyrus_newsroom`), NOT the stdlib-only query Lambda — same place `compute_pagerank` already lives.
- Sits beside the existing `signals concept-report` (`popularity`/`trending`/`pagerank`) as a `--report-type frontier` (or sibling command), so the surface is familiar.
- Output feeds the existing include/exclude gate (PPY-9272c8): a human includes/excludes each suggestion. The report creates no `Reference`, no `Item`, no `EditionItem`, no live wiki page. It is a scout suggestion, not evidence.

**Defer:** core-periphery fit (Alg 3), community-boundary rank (Alg 4) — add only after 1+2 prove useful on the real corpus.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
## 5. Risks (and the hard gate)

1. **Corpus is small — primary risk.** The architecture doc (`project/wiki/knowledge-base-architecture.md`) repeatedly warns the corpus is small because of the human curation gate, and "do not build machinery whose value scales with corpus size while the corpus is small." Periphery shells on a small graph are noisy and unstable: a node can flip shell on a single new edge. **Mitigation:** measure on the current corpus before committing to a UI; report shell number AND a stability indicator (bootstrap over edge perturbation); if the graph is too sparse to produce stable shells, say so in Kanbus and stop — do not force a feature.

2. **A high score must NEVER auto-accept a source.** Human include/exclude remains the gate (PPY-9272c8). The frontier report is a suggestion list, not a citation, not a `Reference`, not an `Item`. Wiki is not evidence (PPY-964472 epic). Fail closed.

3. **Heterogeneous graph → must pick a projection.** Periphery metrics are well-defined on a single undirected projection. We must choose one (drop operational relations via `OPERATIONAL_RELATION_TYPES`; treat `mentions`/`cites`/ontology edges as undirected; weight by `RELATION_WEIGHTS`) and document it. Different projections surface different peripheries — record the chosen projection in the report metadata.

4. **Lambda is stdlib-only; the CLI is not.** Put periphery computation in the CLI/Python tooling path, never in the `knowledge-query` Lambda (which bundles stdlib-only). Mirror where `compute_pagerank` already lives.

5. **Link prediction surfaces spam.** Adamic-Adar/Jaccard over reference↔concept pairs can promote promotional sources that share tokens with core concepts. The human gate handles this; do NOT surface a "confidence" that implies trust. Surface structural adjacency only.

6. **No fake density from embeddings.** The product HAS embeddings (S3 Vectors, `ontology_concept_profile`), but periphery/adjacency is a structural property. Using embeddings would turn this into an LLM-adjacent similarity search — exactly what Ryan excluded. Use graph structure only. (Embeddings allowed only as an optional display tie-breaker, never as the signal.)

7. **Don't ship a second ranking pipeline.** Per the architecture doc's settled decision ("graph traversal is a retriever, not a separate answering mode"), the frontier report is a scout surface feeding the gate, not a fourth retrieval arm fused into `knowledgeQuery`. Keep it out of the query engine's rank fusion.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
## 6. Acceptance shape (Gherkin sketch — PLAN ONLY, not for execution)

This is the behavior the eventual feature would specify. Not implemented now. Ryan says go before any runtime work.

```gherkin
Feature: Non-LLM periphery/adjacency scout for the knowledge graph
  As a researcher,
  I want a quantitative, non-LLM suggestion list of concepts and sources on the outer periphery of the knowledge graph,
  so that I can scout adjacent territory the catalog does not already cluster on — with a human gate, never auto-accepted.

  Scenario: Frontier report ranks outer-shell concepts adjacent to the authority core
    Given the current SemanticNode/SemanticRelation graph for a corpus
    And the existing authorityRank top-K concepts define the accepted core
    When I run `papyrus knowledge signals frontier-report --corpus-key <k> --top 20`
    Then the report lists concepts ranked by periphery score (k-shell + PPR-distance-from-core)
    And each suggestion includes its shell number, PPR-distance, and a stability indicator
    And the report includes "almost connected" reference↔concept pairs from link prediction
    But the report creates no Reference, no Item, no EditionItem, and no live wiki page
    And no suggestion is auto-accepted; every entry awaits a human include/exclude

  Scenario: A sparse or unstable graph fails closed with a finding, not a feature
    Given the graph has too few nodes or unstable shells to produce a meaningful periphery
    When I run the frontier report
    Then it reports the sparsity/instability finding and emits no ranked suggestions
    And the finding is recorded in Kanbus rather than forcing a noisy suggestion list
```

**Status:** open, plan only. No branch of runtime work until Ryan approves. Specs may be written; no production code.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
## Implementation started (Ryan said proceed)

Status moved from plan-only to in_progress. This is now implementation, not a second plan.

### Product (clarified against the code)
A Papyrus tool that lists graph items by **centrality**, so a human can ask for either the MOST central or the LEAST central items — both ends of the same ranking. Shaped as a new `centrality` report type on the existing `papyrus knowledge signals concept-report` CLI, with `--order {most,least}`.

### Honest fit (verified against code, not the hunch-as-spec)
- The hunch said "existing authority/PageRank for the center end, one shared ranking inverted." Verified: `rank_concepts` (`ontology_enrichment.py:476`) already computes weighted PageRank (`compute_pagerank:608`) over the full `SemanticNode`/`SemanticRelation` graph (all non-operational relation types, weighted by `RELATION_WEIGHTS`). It returns a raw `pageRank` per concept. That raw PageRank IS a standard centrality measure — so the centrality ranking reuses that, and `--order least` simply returns the opposite end of the same ranking. No second pipeline, no k-shell needed for v1.
- The existing `signals concept-report` `pagerank` report uses a *different* graph (concept co-mention only, `_weighted_pagerank` in `coverage_theme.py`). Centrality deliberately uses the full-graph authority PageRank instead, because the plan assessed the full SemanticNode/SemanticRelation graph and because the co-mention graph excludes zero-mention/ontology-only concepts — which are exactly the periphery we want visible at the "least" end.
- `centrality` is currently aliased to `pagerank` in `_normalize_concept_report_type`; that alias is being removed so `centrality` is its own report type.

### Fail-closed gate
If the corpus subgraph is too sparse for a stable ranking (no relations among corpus concepts → uniform PageRank, or fewer than a minimum node count), the centrality report emits an empty ranked list with a `stability` block explaining why, rather than inventing scores (the existing `pagerank` report falls back to mention frequency; centrality does NOT).

### Hard gates honored
- No auto-accept. The report creates a `concept_report` Message + `uses_signal` relations only (reuses `build_concept_report_records`); no `Reference`/`Item`/`EditionItem`. Human include/exclude remains the gate.
- No LLM calls, no embeddings. Pure graph structure + PageRank.
- Targets develop. Not merged to main.

Progress will be recorded here as the work lands.
